### A positive matching construction supplies each \(Z_h\)

Split any high-degree parity constraint into a tree of ternary XOR constraints. Auxiliary variables have weight one and a unique completion.

For a ternary constraint, use:

| Required parity | Internal matching gadget |
|---|---|
| Odd | A triangle whose three vertices are external ports |
| Even | A triangle on ports \(a,b\) and an internal vertex \(r\), with the third port attached as a leaf to \(r\) |

Selecting an external matching edge consumes its port. **Each allowed external pattern leaves exactly one internal perfect matching; each forbidden pattern leaves none.**

Connect corresponding ports with edges of activity \(q_e\). Consequently,
\[
\boxed{Z_{\mathrm{PM}}(H_h,q)=Z_h(s).}
\tag{6}
\]

This is an exact, positive, weight-preserving construction. It contains no subtraction of large quantities to obtain a rare logical probability.

The published unweighted FPRAS suffices. For rational activities \(a_e\), clear denominators with \(D\) and write \(W_e=Da_e\). An unweighted two-terminal gadget can realize completion counts \(1,W_e,0\), respectively, when neither, both, or exactly one terminal is consumed internally. Parallel composition adds weights; series composition multiplies them. Binary expansion therefore realizes \(W_e\) using \(O(\log W_e)\) vertices.

For an \(N\)-vertex weighted graph,
\[
\#\mathrm{PM}(H')
=D^{N/2}Z_{\mathrm{PM}}(H,a).
\tag{7}
\]

The expansion is polynomial in the rational input length. Thus neither exponentially small activities nor rare syndromes introduce an inverse-probability enumeration cost.

### Executed construction checks

I executed exact checks of all 28 local parity signatures, 40 rational \(T\)-join/matching partition identities, integer-weight gadgets for weights \(1\) through \(64\), and a complete rational-to-unweighted identity. A separate enumeration of 256 fault histories recovered all eight edge rates from syndrome moments and checked the risk comparison across all 16 detector records.

These verify finite construction identities. **The general FPRAS was not implemented or benchmarked.**
